examples.ko: 사고 현장에서 부상자의 후송이 바로 시작됐어요.
examples.en: At the accident scene, the transfer of the injured began right away.
A helicopter is the fastest way to transfer a patient.
The patient's condition got worse during the transfer.
The doctor decided to transfer the patient to a big hospital.

examples.ko: 응급 후송 차량 때문에 길이 잠깐 막혔어요.
examples.en: The road was blocked for a moment because of an emergency transport vehicle.
On an island, evacuation is difficult when the weather is bad.

explain: '이송'과 비슷하지만, 후송은 전쟁터나 사고·재난 현장에서 다친 사람을 더 안전한 곳이나 큰 병원으로 옮길 때 많이 써요. 병원끼리 환자를 옮길 때는 '이송'이 더 자연스러워요. 일상 대화에서는 '병원으로 옮기다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is similar to '이송' (transfer), but 후송 is often used when an injured person is moved from an accident, disaster or battle site to a safer place or a bigger hospital. When patients are moved between hospitals, '이송' sounds more natural. In daily talk people say '병원으로 옮기다'.

examples.en: The paramedics took the patient to a big hospital.
The helicopter takes the injured person away right away.
How should we evacuate the injured hiker?
The medical team decided to transfer the critical patient to Seoul.
I contacted the rescue team to ask them to evacuate him.
We couldn't evacuate the patient because of the rain.

explain: '옮기다'보다 격식 있는 말이라 뉴스나 보고에서 자주 들려요. 보통 '환자/부상자를 병원으로 후송하다'처럼 대상과 도착지가 같이 나와요. 다친 사람을 주어로 말할 때는 '후송되다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is more formal than '옮기다' (to move) and often heard in news and reports. It usually comes with the person and the destination, like '환자를 병원으로 후송하다'. When the injured person is the subject, use '후송되다'.

examples.en: I felt heavy-hearted after hearing the teacher's admonishment.

examples.ko: 아버지는 긴 훈계 끝에 아들을 용서했어요.
examples.en: After a long lecture, the father forgave his son.
I don't like to listen to preaching that sounds like nagging.
My younger brother came late again despite the warning.
Grandmother gave her grandson a short word of caution.

examples.ko: 훈계만 하지 말고 이유도 들어 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't just lecture me, but listen to my reasons too.

explain: 부모님이나 선생님 같은 윗사람이 잘못을 고치도록 타이르는 말에 써요. '잔소리'는 듣는 사람이 귀찮아하는 느낌이 강하고, '꾸중'은 이미 한 잘못을 혼내는 쪽에 가까워요. 보통 '훈계를 하다/듣다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It is used when someone senior, like a parent or teacher, talks to you to correct your behavior. '잔소리' (nagging) carries an annoyed feeling, and '꾸중' (scolding) is closer to being told off for something you already did. It is usually used as '훈계를 하다/듣다'.

en: discipline; admonish; caution; teach a lesson

examples.en: The teacher quietly admonished the student who was late.

examples.ko: 부모님은 아이를 너무 심하게 훈계하지 않아요.
examples.en: My parents don't lecture the child too harshly.

examples.ko: 사람들 앞에서 후배를 훈계하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't lecture a junior in front of other people.
Grandfather always lectures us to be polite.
Even when I lecture him, the child only pretends to listen.

examples.ko: 그는 친구를 훈계할 만큼 잘난 사람이 아니에요.
examples.en: He is not a person who is good enough to lecture his friends.

explain: 윗사람이 아랫사람에게 잘못을 고치라고 타이를 때 쓰는 말이라, 친구 사이에는 어색해요. 친구에게는 '충고하다'가 자연스럽고, '타이르다'는 더 부드러운 느낌이에요. 훈계 내용이 맞더라도 말투가 길어지면 '잔소리'로 들려요.
explain_en: This is for a senior person telling a junior to correct a mistake, so it sounds awkward between friends. With friends, '충고하다' is more natural, and '타이르다' feels gentler. Even when the content is right, a long lecturing tone gets heard as '잔소리' (nagging).

en: thoracic surgery; department of thoracic surgery

examples.en: You get heart surgery at the thoracic surgery department.

examples.ko: 저희 아버지는 큰 병원 흉부외과 의사세요.
examples.en: My father is a doctor in the thoracic surgery department of a big hospital.
I have a problem with my lung, so I went to thoracic surgery.
The thoracic surgery department at our hospital is always busy.

examples.ko: 이 병원에는 흉부외과 전문의가 세 분 계세요.
examples.en: This hospital has three thoracic surgery specialists.

examples.ko: 내과 의사가 저를 흉부외과에 소개해 줬어요.
examples.en: The internal medicine doctor referred me to thoracic surgery.

explain: 약으로 치료하는 '내과'와 달리, 수술이 필요한 가슴 쪽 문제를 맡는 과예요. 심장이나 폐가 아파도 처음에는 내과에서 진찰받고, 수술이 필요할 때 흉부외과로 이어지는 경우가 많아요. '정형외과', '신경외과'처럼 '~외과' 이름과 같이 기억하면 좋아요.
explain_en: Unlike '내과' (internal medicine), which mostly treats with medicine, this department handles surgery on the chest area. Even for heart or lung trouble, many people first see internal medicine and are sent to thoracic surgery when an operation is needed. It helps to learn it with other '~외과' names like '정형외과' and '신경외과'.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 부모님의 말씀을 거역할 수 없었어요.
examples.en: When I was young, I couldn't go against my parents' words.
He was driven out for defying the king's order.
No one can go against the chairman's will.

examples.ko: 자연의 흐름은 거역해서 좋을 게 없어요.
examples.en: There is nothing good in defying the course of nature.
I want to defy fate, but it isn't easy.
If you disobey your boss's instructions, you'll be in trouble.

explain: 윗사람의 명령이나 운명, 자연처럼 따라야 할 것에 맞서는 느낌이 강해서 무겁고 글 같은 말이에요. 규칙이나 약속은 '어기다', 흐름이나 순리는 '거스르다'가 더 자연스러워요. 일상 대화에서는 '말을 안 듣다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It carries a heavy, written tone of standing against something you are supposed to follow, like a superior's order, fate or nature. For rules and promises, '어기다' is more natural, and for a flow or the natural order, '거스르다' fits better. In daily talk people say '말을 안 듣다'.

examples.en: I went through quarantine at the airport and came out.
Quarantine is strict for fruit brought in from abroad.

examples.ko: 검역 때문에 입국이 한 시간 늦어졌어요.
examples.en: Entry was delayed by an hour because of quarantine.
If you want to bring a puppy in, you need quarantine documents.
I got stopped at quarantine and threw away the meat I brought.
The quarantine office opens early in the morning.

explain: 공항이나 항구에서 병이나 해충이 들어오지 못하게 사람, 동물, 식물, 식품을 확인하는 일이에요. 일반적인 '검사'보다 전염병을 막는 목적이 분명해요. 보통 '검역을 받다', '검역 서류'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is the check at airports and ports on people, animals, plants and food to keep diseases and pests from coming in. Compared with a general '검사' (inspection), the purpose of stopping infection is clear. It is commonly used as '검역을 받다' or '검역 서류'.

examples.en: Airport staff quarantine the animals coming in.
The imported fruit was inspected first at the port.
How many days does it take to quarantine an animal?
The quarantine officer carefully inspected our luggage.

examples.ko: 수입 소고기를 검역한 뒤에 시장에 내놓아요.
examples.en: Imported beef is put on the market after it is inspected.

examples.ko: 입국장에서 사람들을 검역하지 않는 나라도 있어요.
examples.en: Some countries do not quarantine people at the arrival hall.

explain: 검역하는 쪽(검역관, 기관)이 주어일 때 쓰는 말이에요. 검역을 받는 입장에서는 '검역을 받다'라고 해요. 질병을 막는 일이라 '검사하다'보다 범위가 좁고 목적이 분명해요.
explain_en: This is used when the inspecting side, such as an officer or agency, is the subject. From the point of view of the one being checked, you say '검역을 받다'. Because it is about stopping disease, it is narrower and has a clearer purpose than '검사하다'.

examples.ko: 이 마을 사람들은 대부분 쌀 경작으로 먹고살아요.
examples.en: Most people in this village make a living from rice cultivation.
The cultivated area is shrinking every year.
Cultivation is not easy on a mountain slope.
Grandfather hurt his back from long years of farming.
Farmland is disappearing little by little near the city.

examples.ko: 경작에 쓰는 땅은 비가 충분히 와야 좋아요.
examples.en: Land used for cultivation needs enough rain to be good.

explain: 일상에서는 '농사'라고 많이 말하고, 경작은 뉴스나 설명문에서 땅을 일구는 일을 말할 때 나와요. '경작지', '경작 면적'처럼 땅과 함께 쓰는 말이 많아요. '농사'가 일 전체라면 경작은 땅에 초점이 있어요.
explain_en: In daily talk people say '농사' (farming), while 경작 appears in news and written explanations about working the land. It often forms words tied to land, like '경작지' and '경작 면적'. '농사' is the whole job, while 경작 focuses on the land.

examples.en: My father farms a small field himself.

examples.ko: 남의 땅을 빌려 경작하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people rent other people's land and farm it.
In this area, they mainly grow barley.
The ground is dry, so it is hard to cultivate.
In the old days, they cultivated rice fields with cows.

examples.ko: 이 산은 경작하지 않는 땅이라 나무가 많아요.
examples.en: This mountain is uncultivated land, so there are many trees.

explain: 일상에서는 '농사를 짓다'가 더 자연스럽고, 경작하다는 밭이나 논 같은 땅을 목적어로 써서 조금 딱딱하게 들려요. '밭을 경작하다'처럼 땅이 대상이고, 곡식은 '보리를 경작하다'처럼 말할 수도 있어요. 뉴스나 글에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: In daily talk '농사를 짓다' is more natural, and 경작하다 sounds a bit stiff, taking land like a field or paddy as its object. You can say '밭을 경작하다' (cultivate a field), and also '보리를 경작하다' for crops. It appears often in news and writing.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 고위급 회담이 내일 열려요.
examples.en: The high-level talks between the two countries will be held tomorrow.
High-ranking officials have just arrived at the event hall.
I heard the high-ups decided this matter themselves.
A high-ranking official visited the site yesterday.
It's a meeting attended by top officials, so security is strict.
The high-level delegation is scheduled to return in the afternoon.

explain: 뉴스에서 '고위급 회담', '고위급 인사'처럼 뒤에 명사를 붙여 가장 많이 들려요. 회사 이야기보다는 정부나 국가 사이의 일에 더 자주 쓰여요. 반대로 실무자 수준은 '실무급'이라고 해요.
explain_en: You hear it most in the news before a noun, as in '고위급 회담' and '고위급 인사'. It is used more for government and international matters than for company talk. The opposite level, working-level staff, is called '실무급'.

examples.en: The students recited one poem each.
At the graduation ceremony, my friend recites her own poem.
It's easier to memorize if you recite it out loud.
I watched a video of an actor reciting a letter.

examples.ko: 시를 낭송할 때는 천천히 읽어 보세요.
examples.en: When you recite a poem, try reading slowly.
Grandmother used to recite old sijo poems.

explain: '낭독하다'는 글을 소리 내어 읽는 쪽이고, 낭송하다는 시처럼 리듬과 느낌을 살려 읽거나 외워서 들려주는 쪽에 가까워요. 보통 '시를 낭송하다'처럼 시나 글과 같이 나와요. 이름에 쓰는 '시 낭송회'도 자주 들려요.
explain_en: '낭독하다' is closer to reading a text aloud, while 낭송하다 is closer to reading or reciting with rhythm and feeling, as with a poem. It usually comes with poems or literary texts, as in '시를 낭송하다'. You also often hear '시 낭송회' (poetry reading event).

examples.en: I drove stakes into the ground to pitch the tent.
I tied the goat to a stake.
The fence post fell over in the wind.
I stretched a rope tightly between the stakes.
I sharpened the end of the wooden stake.
I marked the boundary of the land with stakes.

explain: 땅에 박아 세우는 굵고 긴 막대를 말해요. '기둥'은 건물을 받치는 것이고, 말뚝은 땅에 박아서 묶거나 표시하는 데 써요. 비유로도 쓰이니 아래 표현도 같이 알아 두세요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 이 회사에 말뚝을 박을 생각인가 봐요.
phrases.en: He seems to be planning to stay at this company for good.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 자리에 오래 눌러 있겠다는 뜻으로 가볍게 쓰는 입말이에요. 칭찬일 수도, 약간 놀리는 말일 수도 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual spoken phrase meaning someone will stay in one place for a long time. It can be praise or mild teasing.
phrases.en_equiv: to put down roots; to plant oneself somewhere for good

explain_en: It is a thick, long stick driven into the ground. A '기둥' (pillar) holds up a building, while a 말뚝 is driven into the ground to tie things to or to mark a place. It is also used figuratively, so see the expression below.

examples.en: The lineage of traditional crafts is in danger of dying out.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 삼 대째 명맥을 이어 오고 있어요.
examples.en: This shop has kept going for three generations.
The small theater troupe barely keeps itself alive.

examples.ko: 그 학교는 명맥도 겨우 이어 가는 처지예요.
examples.en: That school is barely holding on to its existence.

examples.ko: 이 마을 축제는 명맥이 끊겼다가 다시 살아났어요.
examples.en: This village festival died out and then came back to life.
Young craftsmen gathered to keep the tradition alive.

explain: 주로 전통, 기술, 단체처럼 오랫동안 이어져 온 것이 사라지지 않고 남아 있는 상태에 써요. '끊기다', '잇다', '유지하다'와 자주 같이 나와요. 일반적인 '목숨'이나 '존재'보다 '이어져 온 흐름'이라는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is mostly used for something long-lasting, like a tradition, skill or organization, that is still surviving. It often appears with '끊기다' (be cut off), '잇다' (continue) and '유지하다' (maintain). It feels like a continuing line rather than plain '목숨' (life) or '존재' (existence).

examples.en: At the national cemetery, the graves spread out over a wide area.
I visited the cemetery with my family during the holiday.
I bought flowers at the entrance of the cemetery.
We tidied up the area around the cemetery.
Independence activists are enshrined in this cemetery.
The road to the cemetery is steep.

explain: '무덤'이 하나하나의 무덤이라면, 묘역은 무덤이 모여 있는 구역 전체를 말해요. 가족 무덤이 있는 곳은 '산소'라고도 하고, 국립묘지나 공원처럼 넓은 곳은 묘역이라고 많이 불러요. 말투가 조금 공식적이에요.
explain_en: While '무덤' is a single grave, 묘역 is the whole area where graves are gathered. A family grave site is also called '산소', and large places such as national cemeteries or memorial parks are often called 묘역. The tone is a bit formal.

examples.en: I saw a cat roaming the alley late at night.

examples.ko: 아이가 시장 안을 혼자 배회하고 있었어요.
examples.en: The child was wandering around the market alone.

examples.ko: 그 남자는 집 앞을 오래 배회했어요.
examples.en: That man loitered in front of the house for a long time.
A lost puppy is roaming around the neighborhood.

examples.ko: 할 일 없이 거리를 배회하지 말고 집에 가세요.
examples.en: Don't wander the streets with nothing to do. Go home.

examples.ko: 수상한 사람이 학교 주변을 배회한다는 신고가 있었어요.
examples.en: There was a report that a suspicious person was hanging around the school.

explain: 뚜렷한 목적 없이 같은 곳 주변을 이리저리 돌아다닌다는 느낌이고, 조금 부정적으로 들릴 때가 많아요. '서성이다'는 한자리 가까이에서 왔다 갔다 하는 느낌이고, 배회하다는 범위가 더 넓어요. 일상 대화에서는 '돌아다니다'를 더 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It feels like going back and forth around a place with no clear purpose, and it often sounds a bit negative. '서성이다' is pacing close to one spot, while 배회하다 covers a wider area. In daily talk people more often say '돌아다니다'.

examples.ko: 봄이 되자 개울가 버들에 새잎이 났어요.
examples.en: When spring came, new leaves grew on the willows by the stream.
By the stream, the willow sways gently in the wind.

examples.ko: 연못 옆에 버들 한 그루가 서 있어요.
examples.en: A willow tree stands next to the pond.
The children made a whistle from willow branches.

examples.ko: 강가에 버들이 줄지어 서 있어서 풍경이 예뻐요.
examples.en: Willows stand in a row along the river, so the scenery is pretty.
A single willow leaf fell onto the water.

explain: 일상에서는 '버드나무'라고 말하는 경우가 많고, 버들은 시나 노래, '버들가지', '버들잎' 같은 말에서 자주 보여요. 가지가 길게 늘어진 나무는 '수양버들'이라고 해요. 부드럽고 가는 느낌을 줘서 글에서 풍경을 그릴 때 어울려요.
explain_en: In daily life people often say '버드나무', while 버들 shows up in poems, songs and words like '버들가지' (willow branch) and '버들잎' (willow leaf). The kind with long hanging branches is called '수양버들' (weeping willow). It gives a soft, slender feel, so it suits descriptions of scenery in writing.

examples.en: This museum has a very wide variety of items in its collection.
We lent my father's collection to the exhibition.
My most treasured item is an old stamp.

examples.ko: 미술관 소장품 중에서 이 그림이 제일 유명해요.
examples.en: Among the museum's collection, this painting is the most famous.
Part of the collection was damaged in the fire.

examples.ko: 개인 소장품이라 사진을 찍으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: It's a personal collection item, so you can't take photos.

explain: 박물관이나 미술관, 또는 개인이 가지고 보관하는 물건에 써요. '수집품'은 모은 물건이라는 점이 강하고, 소장품은 자기가 가지고 있다는 점이 강해요. '소장하다'와 같이 기억하면 좋아요.
explain_en: It is used for items kept by a museum, an art gallery or an individual. '수집품' stresses that the things were collected, while 소장품 stresses that someone owns and holds them. It helps to learn it together with '소장하다'.

examples.en: Orders poured in after the broadcast aired.

examples.ko: 티켓 문의 전화가 하루 종일 쇄도해요.
examples.en: Calls asking about tickets keep flooding in all day.
Complaint emails flooded in, so the staff were busy.
Reservations for the new product are pouring in.

examples.ko: 사연이 쇄도하면 다 읽지 못할 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If stories pour in, we may not be able to read them all.

examples.ko: 도움을 주겠다는 연락이 쇄도할 줄은 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I didn't expect offers of help to flood in.

explain: 주문, 문의, 전화, 신청처럼 요청이 한꺼번에 많이 들어올 때 써요. 뉴스나 기사에서 자주 보이는 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '밀려들다', '몰려들다'가 더 부드러워요.
explain_en: It is used when many requests, such as orders, inquiries, calls or applications, come in all at once. You often see it in news articles. In daily conversation, '밀려들다' and '몰려들다' sound softer.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 댐 수문을 열었어요.
examples.en: It rained a lot, so they opened the dam's floodgates.
When the floodgate opened, water gushed out.

examples.ko: 수문 개방 시간을 방송으로 알려 줘요.
examples.en: They announce the floodgate opening time by broadcast.

examples.ko: 수문 근처는 위험하니까 가까이 가지 마세요.
examples.en: It's dangerous near the floodgate, so please don't go close.

examples.ko: 강 하류에는 수문이 세 개 있어요.
examples.en: There are three floodgates downstream on the river.

examples.ko: 수문 관리 직원이 물 높이를 확인했어요.
examples.en: The floodgate staff checked the water level.

explain: 댐, 저수지, 방조제에서 물의 양을 조절하는 문이에요. '둑'은 물을 막는 구조물 자체이고, 수문은 그 안에서 열고 닫는 문이에요. 보통 '수문을 열다/닫다'로 말하고, 홍수 뉴스에서 많이 들려요.
explain_en: It is the gate that controls the amount of water at dams, reservoirs and seawalls. A '둑' is the embankment that holds back water, while a 수문 is the door in it that opens and closes. It is usually used as '수문을 열다/닫다' and is often heard in flood news.

examples.ko: 이 사건이 두 사람이 멀어진 시발점이었어요.
examples.en: This incident was the starting point of the two growing apart.
Seoul Station is the starting point of this line.

examples.ko: 작은 오해가 큰 싸움의 시발점이 됐어요.
examples.en: A small misunderstanding became the start of a big fight.
It takes about an hour from the starting point to the terminus.

examples.ko: 시발점에서 버스를 타면 앉아서 갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you board the bus at the starting point, you can sit down.
I still don't know what the starting point of the change was.

explain: 버스나 지하철이 출발하는 곳, 그리고 어떤 일이 시작된 계기를 말할 때 써요. '출발점'은 더 넓게 쓰이고, 시발점은 노선의 시작이나 일이 커진 계기를 말할 때 자주 들려요. 반대말은 '종점'이에요.
explain_en: It is used for the place where a bus or subway starts, and for the trigger that began a bigger event. '출발점' is used more broadly, while 시발점 is often heard for the start of a route or the cause that set something off. Its opposite is '종점' (terminus).

examples.en: This sea is famous as a squid fishing ground.
The fishing ground is far, so the boat takes several days.
After the typhoon passed, the fish in the fishing ground decreased.

examples.ko: 새로운 어장을 찾으려고 어부들이 먼 바다로 나갔어요.
examples.en: The fishermen went out to the far sea to find a new fishing ground.

examples.ko: 어장 근처에서는 낚시를 하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not fish near the fishing ground.
Many boats go back and forth between fishing grounds.

explain: 물고기를 잡는 바다나 강의 구역을 말하고, '어촌', '어부'와 같이 바다 일을 말할 때 나와요. 양식하는 곳은 '양식장'이라고 해서 서로 달라요. 비유 표현도 있어서 아래에서 같이 알아 두세요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 어장 관리를 한다고 친구들이 말해요.
phrases.en: My friends say that person keeps several people on the hook.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음이 없으면서 여러 사람이 자기를 좋아하게 두고 관심을 주는 행동을 말하는 입말이에요. 보통 비판하는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A spoken phrase for keeping several people interested without really having feelings for them. It is usually critical.

explain_en: It refers to the sea or river area where fish are caught, and appears with words like '어촌' (fishing village) and '어부' (fisherman). A place where fish are farmed is called '양식장', which is different. It also has a figurative use, so see below.

examples.en: The judging must be strict for everyone to trust the result.
The judge ruled on the case strictly.
The exam supervision was strict, so there was no cheating.
We selected the applicants with strict standards.

examples.ko: 그 선생님은 성적 처리가 아주 엄정해요.
examples.en: That teacher is very strict in handling grades.
An evaluation that isn't strict leads to complaints.

explain: 심사, 수사, 평가, 판단처럼 공정함이 중요한 일에 쓰는 격식 있는 말이에요. 부모님이나 선생님의 성격이 무섭고 엄격하다고 할 때는 '엄하다'나 '엄격하다'가 더 자연스러워요. 뉴스에서는 '엄정하게 처리하다'가 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a formal word for matters where fairness is important, such as judging, investigation, evaluation and decisions. To say a parent's or teacher's personality is stern, '엄하다' or '엄격하다' sounds more natural. In the news you often hear '엄정하게 처리하다' (handle strictly).

examples.en: He was caught trying to destroy the evidence.

examples.ko: 회사 서류를 인멸한 직원이 조사를 받아요.
examples.en: The employee who destroyed company documents is being investigated.

examples.ko: 자료를 인멸하면 더 큰 처벌을 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you destroy the data, you could receive a heavier punishment.
He was suspected of destroying evidence.

examples.ko: 기록을 인멸하지 못하도록 컴퓨터를 먼저 확인했어요.
examples.en: We checked the computer first so that they couldn't destroy the records.

examples.ko: 누가 문서를 인멸하라고 시켰는지 밝혀야 해요.
examples.en: We have to find out who told them to destroy the documents.

explain: 거의 '증거를 인멸하다'처럼 범죄나 수사 이야기에서 흔적을 없앤다는 뜻으로 나와요. 뉴스나 법 관련 글에서 보이는 딱딱한 말이에요. 일상에서 파일이나 물건을 없앨 때는 '지우다', '없애다'를 써요.
explain_en: It mostly appears in crime and investigation stories, as in '증거를 인멸하다', meaning to erase traces. It is a stiff word seen in news and legal writing. For everyday deleting or getting rid of files or things, use '지우다' or '없애다'.
